Caller supplied PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` in place of Steps 0 and 1. The process cwd never changes. Every path below is carried as a value.

## Variant A: home worktree exists at eeeeeee

**Resolve ROOT and home**
1. cwd `/work/widget`: `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir` returns `/work/widget/.git` twice, so `ROOT=/work/widget`.
2. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` returns empty, so this is not a submodule.
3. Overrides contain only the runner, with no `## using-git-worktrees` keys. There is no native tool or wrapper.
4. `NAME=fix-retry` and `WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
5. Home is #12 on `fix/retry`, so `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
6. `MEMBER_HEADS` = [#13 fix/cap bbbb…, #14 fix/retry-docs cccc…].

**Fetch and check heads**
7. `git -C /work/widget fetch origin` succeeds.
8. For each admitted PR:
   - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q <head>^{commit}` succeeds for aaaa…, bbbb… and cccc….
   - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry`, `origin/fix/cap` and `origin/fix/retry-docs` each equal the supplied head.
9. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main` gives `BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`.

**Ordered stops**
10. No PR is fork-hosted.
11. `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain` shows `fix/retry` only at the selected home, which is not "another path."
12. Heads are reachable. The N=1 ancestry row does not apply.

**Recover interrupted member merges**
13. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse refs/heads/fix/retry` gives `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`.
14. `git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaa… eeee…` exits 0.
15. `git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaa…..eeee…` returns one entry: eeee…, parents aaaa… bbbb…, subject "merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12". This entry is valid:
    - It has two parents.
    - #13 is an admitted member.
    - bbbbbbb matches #13's original head.
    - The second parent is #13's full original `headRefOid`.
    - The subject is canonical.
16. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` returns empty, so the tree is clean.
17. Record `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)`. No new commit is made.

**Provision**
18. Recovery row: reuse the clean selected worktree unchanged. There is no update-ref, `-b`, reset, clean or deletion.
19. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns eeee…, which equals the validated tip.

**Merge remaining members**
20. Saved last-good SHA is eeee….
21. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12" cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc` creates fffffff. Record `Member merge: #14 fffffff`.

**Merge the base**
22. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main` produces a clean merge. Record `merge: 1111111`.
23. Prove each original head is in final HEAD. Each `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor <head> HEAD` exits 0 for aaaa…, bbbb… and cccc….

**Threads**
24. I run the reviewThreads `gh api graphql --paginate …` query with `-F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=12`, then `n=13`, then `n=14`. Each returns empty, so I record `Threads: none` for each.

**Read-back**
25. `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain` prints `worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
26. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry branch --show-current` prints `fix/retry`.

**Step 4 report**
```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ eeeeeee
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)
Member merge: #14 fffffff
merge: 1111111
Threads: none (#12, #13, #14)
Ready to implement the retry-cap rework
```

## Variant A-no-worktree: local branch at eeeeeee, no worktree

**Steps 1–12:** identical to Variant A. In step 11, `worktree list --porcelain` shows no checkout of `fix/retry` anywhere.

**Recover**
13–15. Identical to A:
- `rev-parse refs/heads/fix/retry` returns the local tip eeee….
- Ancestry from aaaa… exits 0.
- The first-parent walk validates only eeeeeee as the canonical #13 merge.

16. There is no existing tree to dirt-check. The fresh-creation source check, `git -C /work/widget status --porcelain`, returns empty, so the source is clean.

17. Record `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)`.

**Provision (recovery row, no worktree)**
18. `git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees` succeeds, so `.worktrees` is already ignored.
19. `git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry` checks out the existing branch. There is no `-b`, update-ref, reset or deletion.
20. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns eeee…, which equals the validated local tip.

**Steps 21–27:** identical to A:
- #14 merges with `-m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12"` as fffffff.
- The base merges as 1111111.
- Ancestry proofs for aaaa…, bbbb… and cccc… exit 0.
- Threads are none.
- Read-back prints `worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` and branch `fix/retry`.

**Step 4 report:** identical to Variant A's report, starting `Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`, `Base: fix/retry @ eeeeeee`, with the same PR, pre-rework, Base SHA, member, merge and threads lines.

## Variant B: extra unrelated commit

**Resolve ROOT and home**
1. cwd is the session's linked worktree `other`. `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir` returns `/work/widget/.git/worktrees/other` and `/work/widget/.git`.
2. `ROOT=/work/widget`, derived from the common dir. The caller's tree `other` (HEAD 9999999) is not the selected home on `fix/retry`, so it is not adopted and not inspected for recovery.
3. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` returns empty.
4. Home is `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.

**Fetch and stops**
5. `git -C /work/widget fetch origin` succeeds. Per-head reachability and remote-equality checks pass for all three PRs.
6. `BASE_SHA=dddd…`.
7. No ordered stop fires.

**Recover**
8. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse refs/heads/fix/retry` returns 2222222…. This is the actual local home tip, not caller HEAD 9999999.
9. `git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaa… 2222222…` exits 0.
10. `git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaa…..2222222…` returns:
    - `2222222… eeee… unrelated cleanup` (single parent, not a canonical member merge)
    - `eeee… aaaa… bbbb… merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12`

**Stop before any write.** The unrelated commit fails recovery validation:
```
worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry on fix/retry carries commits beyond PR #12's head (aaaaaaa) that are not member merges from this list; resolve by hand or remove the worktree.
```

Nothing further runs:
- No worktree add, reset, rebase, deletion or merge.
- No thread fetch.
- No Step 4 report.

I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

These are three independent synthetic runs. Every command below runs with **cwd `/work/widget`**; no `cd` is run. Commands targeting the selected tree use `git -C`. The caller’s explicit root takes precedence over session isolation, including in B.

Resolved inputs:

```text
ROOT=/work/widget
BRANCH=fix/retry
NAME=fix-retry
WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
MEMBER_HEADS:
  #13 fix/cap        bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
  #14 fix/retry-docs cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
baseRefName=main
```

The supplied configuration establishes the selected home and absence of a creator wrapper or applicable worktree override. None of the admitted heads is fork-hosted. Generic linked-worktree reuse does not apply to this PR-head invocation.

## Common preflight — executed independently in each variant

Commands, in order:

```sh
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree
git -C /work/widget fetch origin
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget rev-parse refs/heads/fix/retry
```

Root metadata resolves to the primary repository, not a submodule. Every original head exists and equals its remote branch. Resolve:

```text
BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd
```

There is no conflicting checkout of `fix/retry`: A has it at the selected home; A-no-worktree and B have none. B’s unrelated session checkout is not adopted.

## A — recover the selected existing worktree

The local-branch inspection resolves `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`, independently of caller HEAD.

```sh
git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

Ancestry succeeds. The sole walked commit is the stipulated two-parent canonical #13 merge; its second parent is #13’s original full head. Status is empty and HEAD equals the validated local tip. Reuse this tree unchanged.

Record `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)`. Do not merge #13 again.

Continue with the shared completion below.

## A-no-worktree — recover the local branch, then provision it

The local-branch inspection again resolves `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`.

```sh
git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
git -C /work/widget status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees
git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

The walk validates the same canonical #13 merge. The primary is clean. The ignore check succeeds, so no ignore-file write is needed. Creation checks out the **existing validated branch**, without `-b`, `update-ref`, or resetting it. Selected-home HEAD equals the full `eeee…` tip.

Record `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)`.

## Shared completion — executed separately for A and A-no-worktree

```sh
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m 'merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12' cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
```

#14 merges as `fffffff`; the base merges cleanly as `1111111`. All three provenance checks succeed. Read-backs confirm the selected home and exact branch.

## B — exact pre-write refusal

After common preflight, local `fix/retry` resolves to the stipulated `2222222` tip, not session HEAD `9999999`.

```sh
git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa refs/heads/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..refs/heads/fix/retry
```

Ancestry succeeds, but the walk includes single-parent `2222222`, subject `unrelated cleanup`. Stop before provisioning or merging:

> worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry on fix/retry carries commits beyond PR #12's head (aaaaaaa) that are not member merges from this list; resolve by hand or remove the worktree.

```text
Preserved created legs: none
```

No Step 4 ready report is emitted for B. No tracker calls, tests, spec/plan writes, pushes, closes, resets, rebases, or deletions occur.
